R7AB-moose-atv-0002.name: 250 m E of Huble Creek
R7AB-moose-atv-0002.pressureWhy: No town, pavement or rec site within 1 km and not behind a closure (estimate).
R7AB-moose-atv-0002.parkWhat: where the truck road ends (Cp 15K,16C, Amend 3); unload the ATV (all terrain vehicle)

evidence.t: 20 wetlands within 2 km; nearest 6.4 ha, right here.
Cutblock harvested 2017 (9 years old), 60 m S: browse.

plan: Drive: from City of Prince George, about 99 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate). Via Hwy 97 (Hart Hwy), Northwood Pulpmill Rd, industrial access, Beaver Forest Rd.
Park: 54.14222, -121.66063, where the truck road ends (Cp 15K,16C, Amend 3); unload the ATV (all terrain vehicle). Map links below.
Ride: 3.1 km on unnamed roads and trails by ATV (all terrain vehicle) or 4x4 on rough road, estimate. Then walk 260 m SE, climb about 0 m.
Hunt: moose, Sept, Oct, Nov (season rows). Glass the wetland and cutblock edges at dawn and dusk. Move slowly, stop often (Tip).
Use: .308 Winchester, 165 to 180 grain premium bullet, shots inside about 200 m (219 yd) (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 7-17, Region 7A. Season rows below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-16, private land 2026-10-05, closures 2026-10-16.
R7AB-moose-atv-0002.popWhy: Popular (more hunters): MU 7-17: about 1,422 hunter days a year for moose (2020 to 2024 mean), 0.52 days per square km, top third of BC MUs; access: average access. Estimate, about 50% sure (my pick).

tags.label: Good for 2
tags.why: Cover edge here (cutblock or burn): one hunter sits at a crossing or glasses, the other walks the edge slowly with the wind at their back toward the stander. Agree zones of fire, a meeting point and a time at the truck (Tip, lesson: Hunting with a partner). Pushes are on foot only (99%, synopsis page 11, item 25).

tags.label: Good solo
tags.why: Short pack out: 0.3 km and about 0 m of climb from the parking (Tip). Cell coverage is not in the data: leave a trip plan and carry SOS or a satellite messenger (lesson: Bush safety).
